claims.text: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.InvokeAsync has three catch clauses in this order: KeyNotFoundException -> LogWarning + 404 with ex.Message as detail; ArgumentException -> LogWarning + 400 with ex.Message as detail; Exception -> LogError + 500 with the fixed detail "something went wrong".
C# tries a try block's catch clauses in the order they are written; the first clause whose type matches the thrown exception (or a base type of it) runs, and no later clause is tried.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference, the try-catch-finally statement, catch clause ordering

claims.text: Program.cs calls app.UseMiddleware<ExceptionHandlingMiddleware>() before app.UseMiddleware<RequestLoggingMiddleware>(), so ExceptionHandlingMiddleware is the outermost of the two, registered first.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: DonHang.Api/Program.cs (UseMiddleware calls near the top of the pipeline)

claims.text: WriteProblemAsync sets only Status, Title, Detail on ProblemDetails (no Type/Instance). It sets ContentType to application/problem+json, but WriteAsJsonAsync overwrites that to application/json - body has the Problem Details shape, not the media type.

claims.text: Without this middleware, an unhandled exception skips the app's own Problem Details shape: in Development (what docker-compose.yml sets), WebApplication's default developer exception page returns a 500 with the stack trace; elsewhere the host's own bare 500.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs, ASP.NET Core error handling, developer exception page default-enablement conditions

claims.text: LogWarning vs LogError here is this app's own convention, not a framework rule: this middleware calls LogWarning for the two failure shapes it has a specific catch for (KeyNotFoundException, ArgumentException) and LogError only from the generic catch.

In the Development environment, WebApplication enables the developer exception page by default, added outermost (before UseRouting and before any of the app's own middleware) - so it wraps ExceptionHandlingMiddleware, not the other way around.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs, ASP.NET Core middleware order, developer exception page and UseRouting default placement
